Title: Time-since-fire reburn probability surfaces
Novelty_Justification: No gridded reburn probability product exists despite ecological basis from Tepley and Whitman
Tractability_Justification: Clean data (CanadaFireSat + NBAC) with well-defined prediction target and established ML methods
Feasibility_Justification: All data open; Landsat archive + fire perimeters freely available; no fieldwork required initially; modest compute
Confidence_Justification: Ecological relationship well-established (fuel recovery → reburn); main risk is spatial heterogeneity across ecoregions
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Direct fire management application; would inform resource pre-positioning and fuel break prioritization
Skill_Fit_Justification: Classic remote sensing + ML pipeline: Landsat time series + LightGBM/RF + spatial cross-validation

Title: Overwintering fire detection from pre-greenup imagery
Novelty_Justification: Nobody has attempted pre-greenup detection of overwintering fires from satellite; genuinely unexploited phenological window
Tractability_Justification: Signal from underground smoldering may be weak from space; labeled positives are scarce (dozens of confirmed events)
Feasibility_Justification: Sentinel-2 data available but needs Baltzer group collaboration for field validation; few labeled examples limits supervised learning
Confidence_Justification: High null-result risk: spectral signal from subsurface smoldering may be undetectable at 10 m resolution
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Quantifies a poorly understood fire pathway but overwintering fires are a small fraction of total reburns
Skill_Fit_Justification: Remote sensing change detection is core skill but needs field validation expertise and ecological interpretation

Title: Conifer-to-deciduous conversion mapping
Novelty_Justification: Zheng et al. 2024 demonstrated the approach for one megafire; this is scaling + integration with needleleaf index rather than invention
Tractability_Justification: Landsat archive is clean; spectral unmixing well-established; needleleaf index provides improved spectral tool
Feasibility_Justification: Open data throughout; ABoVE provides validation; moderate compute for pan-boreal unmixing
Confidence_Justification: Conifer/deciduous spectral separation well-established; link between conversion rate and reburn probability needs testing but is plausible
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Directly informs whether boreal forest is undergoing irreversible vegetation type conversion — major ecological question
Skill_Fit_Justification: Spectral unmixing + time series analysis + classification: strong remote sensing skill set

Title: 10 m treeline ecotone from ICESat-2 + Sentinel-2
Novelty_Justification: Fusion approaches exist (2025 MAE 1.42 m) but not at ecotone-gradient structural level mapping height + cover + density
Tractability_Justification: ICESat-2 and Sentinel-2 data open; deep learning regression is established; ALS validation from national surveys available
Feasibility_Justification: Needs ALS validation data (available from SLU and Luke); moderate compute; no fieldwork for initial product
Confidence_Justification: ICESat-2 ecotone study (88% detection) and prior fusion work suggest signal is there; main risk is sparse ICESat-2 coverage at ecotone
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Ecotone mapping is scientifically important for understanding treeline dynamics but indirect short-term conservation impact
Skill_Fit_Justification: Deep learning regression + multi-sensor fusion + satellite data processing: core ML/RS skill set

Title: Treeline advance rate from 40-year Landsat
Novelty_Justification: Berner and Feng produced input maps; this is trend analysis on existing data products rather than methodological novelty
Tractability_Justification: Clean Landsat archive; BFAST is established and well-documented; ERA5 for attribution readily available
Feasibility_Justification: Fully open data; low-moderate compute; no fieldwork needed for initial analysis
Confidence_Justification: Landsat NDVI trends in the ecotone are measurable; attribution to climate drivers is harder but feasible at ecoregion scale
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Advance rates are the fundamental input that treeline-shift and carbon models need; quantifies a key climate indicator
Skill_Fit_Justification: Time series analysis + satellite data + trend detection + climate attribution: well-matched skill set

Title: Krummholz detection from VHR satellite imagery
Novelty_Justification: Nobody has mapped individual krummholz patches from satellite; genuinely novel application of object detection to treeline front
Tractability_Justification: VHR commercial data is expensive and limited coverage; krummholz patches are small and visually ambiguous at sub-meter scale
Feasibility_Justification: Requires VHR satellite data access (costly); drone campaigns for training data; field GPS surveys; partnership-dependent
Confidence_Justification: May work for large krummholz patches but miss small ones; scale of objects pushes even VHR resolution limits
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Scientifically interesting as earliest detectable signal of treeline advance but limited direct conservation application
Skill_Fit_Justification: Object detection is strong ML skill but needs field access and ecological interpretation of what counts as krummholz

Title: SAR-optical fusion for sub-100 ha fire detection
Novelty_Justification: SAR-optical fusion for burned area exists conceptually but not specifically implemented for small boreal fire detection
Tractability_Justification: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 open data; NBAC fire perimeters as labels; dual-encoder architectures well-established
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; moderate compute; need to handle cloud masking and missing-modality fusion but this is a solved engineering problem
Confidence_Justification: SAR backscatter change for fire is demonstrated but noisy for small fires; the cloud-gap filling value is real but accuracy uncertain
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Detecting missing 50% of burned area has direct carbon accounting and fire management implications
Skill_Fit_Justification: Multi-sensor deep learning with attention masking: core ML/remote sensing skill set

Title: Sentinel-3 SLSTR night-time thermal fire detection
Novelty_Justification: SLSTR fire products exist for tropics but not optimized for high-latitude boreal; dual-view advantage unexploited
Tractability_Justification: SLSTR at 1 km is coarse for small fires; dual-view adds complexity; thermal fire detection well-understood algorithmically
Feasibility_Justification: Open Sentinel-3 data; ESA archive accessible; moderate compute; standard algorithm development
Confidence_Justification: 1 km resolution means small fires still likely missed; the advantage over VIIRS 375 m is uncertain and may be marginal
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Incremental temporal coverage improvement over VIIRS rather than transformative for fire monitoring
Skill_Fit_Justification: Algorithm development on thermal satellite data; less ML-heavy than other ideas but computationally focused

Title: Prescribed burn verification in Fennoscandia
Novelty_Justification: Nobody has applied satellite monitoring to verify outcomes of conservation prescribed burns in boreal Fennoscandia
Tractability_Justification: Sentinel-2 time series clean and available; prescribed burn locations documented by Luke and Swedish forestry agencies
Feasibility_Justification: Open satellite data; need agency collaboration for burn records and field assessment data but agencies are receptive
Confidence_Justification: Low-intensity burns produce subtle spectral signal; but multi-year trajectory analysis should be detectable at 10 m
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Important for Fennoscandian conservation management but geographically narrow; limited global relevance
Skill_Fit_Justification: Satellite time series analysis and classification; less computationally demanding but well-matched

Title: NISAR L-band InSAR in forested discontinuous permafrost
Novelty_Justification: First satellite L-band InSAR in forested permafrost; NISAR creates an opportunity that did not exist before 2026
Tractability_Justification: InSAR processing in forested terrain technically challenging: coherence maintenance + atmospheric + ionospheric artifacts at L-band
Feasibility_Justification: NISAR data open but InSAR time series processing requires specialized expertise and significant compute; need borehole validation
Confidence_Justification: UAVSAR proof-of-concept encouraging but airborne ≠ satellite (different baselines and geometry); L-band coherence in dense boreal forest unproven from orbit
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Landscape-scale permafrost monitoring has major climate and carbon implications; fills a fundamental measurement gap
Skill_Fit_Justification: InSAR processing is specialized remote sensing skill with steep learning curve but computationally focused

Title: Multi-sensor permafrost vulnerability mapping
Novelty_Justification: Individual sensors applied to permafrost but InSAR + optical + thermal fusion for vulnerability classification not published for forested terrain
Tractability_Justification: Multiple data streams to spatiotemporally harmonize; permafrost state classification (stable/degrading/thawed) requires expert labeling
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; moderate compute; need permafrost domain expert for labeling and validation of vulnerability categories
Confidence_Justification: Multi-sensor fusion should improve over single-sensor but added value needs demonstration; risk of marginal improvement
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Vulnerability maps directly inform infrastructure planning and conservation in permafrost regions
Skill_Fit_Justification: Multi-sensor fusion + ML classification: core skill set; strong computational angle

Title: Fire-permafrost interaction mapping from InSAR
Novelty_Justification: InSAR measurement of post-fire subsidence acceleration at satellite scale not demonstrated; bridges fire and permafrost problems
Tractability_Justification: Same InSAR challenges as BF-06-i plus complexity of fire effects on surface coherence; charred surfaces may improve or degrade signal
Feasibility_Justification: Dependent on NISAR data quality; needs fire perimeter data and partnership with Veraverbeke/Zwieback groups; multi-year timeline
Confidence_Justification: Field studies confirm the effect exists; satellite detection uncertain but if fire scars improve coherence that itself is a useful finding
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Fire-permafrost feedback is a major positive feedback loop in the climate system; quantifying it at scale has high value
Skill_Fit_Justification: InSAR + fire science intersection; specialized but computationally focused

Title: NISAR L-band windthrow severity mapping
Novelty_Justification: L-band SAR for windthrow severity classification is physically motivated but untested
Tractability_Justification: NISAR data open; storm events frequent in Fennoscandia; national forest inventory and ALS provide reference data
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; moderate compute; need ALS damage maps for training labels which are available from Luke and SLU
Confidence_Justification: L-band should provide complementary structural information via volume scattering but improvement over C-band uncertain
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Storm damage detection is operationally useful for salvage planning but ecological impact is modest
Skill_Fit_Justification: SAR processing + classification: core remote sensing skill set

Title: Near-real-time windthrow alerting pipeline
Novelty_Justification: Underlying SAR change detection methods established; novelty is in the operational pipeline and triggering mechanism
Tractability_Justification: Sentinel-1 data streaming; well-defined signal (backscatter change after storm); z-score anomaly detection straightforward
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; requires software engineering for operational pipeline; need agency partnership for end-use deployment
Confidence_Justification: Sentinel-1 windthrow detection demonstrated at 0.88 producer accuracy; the operational wrapping is engineering not research
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Reduces bark beetle outbreak risk through faster salvage logging; operationally important but ecologically modest impact
Skill_Fit_Justification: Data engineering + remote sensing + operational system building: good ML-adjacent skill set

Title: Boreal BirdNET fine-tuning with circumpolar data
Novelty_Justification: BirdNET fine-tuning demonstrated for other regions (Italian Alps 2025); applying to circumpolar boreal is regional transfer not methodological novelty
Tractability_Justification: BirdNET open-source; training data available from Xeno-canto and Luomus archives; fine-tuning pipeline well-documented
Feasibility_Justification: Open models and data; moderate compute; need audio expertise and species identification skills for quality control
Confidence_Justification: Fine-tuning reliably improves BirdNET for regional applications (demonstrated multiple times across biomes)
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Enables scalable biodiversity monitoring in boreal but impact depends on subsequent deployment and adoption
Skill_Fit_Justification: Transfer learning + audio ML + model fine-tuning: strong ML skill fit

Title: Foundation model multi-taxon boreal classifier
Novelty_Justification: Multi-taxon boreal acoustic classifier does not exist; foundation model approach for boreal audio is novel
Tractability_Justification: Foundation models are new and performance on boreal audio uncertain; multi-taxon labeling harder than bird-only
Feasibility_Justification: Foundation models are open (some); multi-taxon training data harder to assemble; mammal and amphibian audio data much scarcer than bird
Confidence_Justification: Foundation models may not outperform BirdNET for birds; added value for non-bird taxa is speculative until tested
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Multi-taxon monitoring captures broader biodiversity information; moves beyond bird-centric assessment
Skill_Fit_Justification: Foundation models + transfer learning + audio ML: strong ML skill set; cutting-edge methods

Title: Acoustic phenology as climate indicator
Novelty_Justification: Acoustic phenology in boreal forests is genuinely novel; 2024 PNAS paper established the concept but no boreal application exists
Tractability_Justification: Requires multi-year continuous PAM data (3+ years minimum); phenological event detection hard to automate for non-bird taxa
Feasibility_Justification: Need long-term PAM deployments (may need to set up new ones); partnership with phenology networks required; multi-year timeline
Confidence_Justification: Concept is scientifically interesting but link between acoustic phenology and ecological process phenology is speculative
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Novel climate indicator but acoustic phenology alone does not drive conservation decisions directly
Skill_Fit_Justification: Time series analysis + event detection + some audio ML: reasonable skill match

Title: IFL fragmentation risk forecasting
Novelty_Justification: No forward-looking IFL fragmentation model exists; all current monitoring is retrospective
Tractability_Justification: Multiple data sources to integrate; fire projections inherently uncertain; model validation limited by short IFL monitoring period (2000-2020)
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; moderate compute; fire projections from CMIP6 available; but need infrastructure and concession boundary data
Confidence_Justification: Forecasting 10-30 years with fire + climate + infrastructure is inherently uncertain; 7-year holdout validation is weak
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Proactive IFL protection has major conservation value; shifting from reactive documentation to predictive planning
Skill_Fit_Justification: Spatiotemporal ML + scenario analysis: computationally focused but requires conservation planning domain knowledge

Title: Connectivity-optimized IFL protection planning
Novelty_Justification: Zonation applied to boreal retention forestry but not specifically to IFL connectivity under climate-driven fire change
Tractability_Justification: Zonation 5 available with corridor algorithms; input data (IFL boundaries + protected areas + species habitat) all available
Feasibility_Justification: Software available and documented; data open; moderate effort; need species habitat models which exist for caribou and wolverine
Confidence_Justification: Zonation is well-validated for conservation planning; connectivity analysis is standard spatial ecology
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Direct conservation planning application; identifies actionable protection priorities with clear policy relevance
Skill_Fit_Justification: Conservation planning software rather than heavy ML; more GIS and spatial optimization than deep learning

Title: SAR-based active fire perimeter tracking
Novelty_Justification: SAR fire monitoring demonstrated for individual events but not systematically for boreal fire progression mapping
Tractability_Justification: SAR backscatter change for fire is noisier than thermal/optical; perimeter delineation from SAR harder than from infrared
Feasibility_Justification: Open Sentinel-1 data; NBAC perimeters for training/validation; moderate compute
Confidence_Justification: SAR fire detection has lower accuracy than thermal; may provide supplementary rather than primary perimeters; value is gap-filling
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Improved fire progression data enables better spread prediction training; indirect but real impact on fire management
Skill_Fit_Justification: SAR processing + deep learning segmentation: core remote sensing/ML skill set

Title: Pan-boreal next-day fire risk with GNN
Novelty_Justification: GNN for fire exists (FireCastNet) but not at pan-boreal next-day resolution with landscape connectivity encoding
Tractability_Justification: Pan-boreal data assembly is large effort; GNN on landscape graph computationally expensive; BCWildfire covers BC only
Feasibility_Justification: Assembling pan-boreal fire data from multiple agencies and formats is a major data engineering challenge; large compute needed
Confidence_Justification: GNNs show promise for spatial prediction; generalization across fire regimes (Shield vs. boreal plains vs. Fennoscandia) is the key risk
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Operational fire risk prediction has direct safety and resource management benefits across the boreal zone
Skill_Fit_Justification: Graph neural networks + spatiotemporal deep learning: strong and current ML skill set

Title: Compositional recovery from spectral unmixing time series
Novelty_Justification: Zheng et al. 2024 demonstrated for one megafire; this is pan-boreal scaling plus needleleaf index integration
Tractability_Justification: Landsat archive clean; spectral unmixing well-established; needleleaf index (2025) provides improved conifer detection
Feasibility_Justification: Open data throughout; ABoVE for validation (1538 sites); moderate compute for pan-boreal processing
Confidence_Justification: Conifer/deciduous spectral separation well-established; compositional recovery tracking works for Zheng's site and should transfer
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Directly informs whether burned forests are recovering to pre-fire composition or permanently converting — major ecological question
Skill_Fit_Justification: Spectral analysis + time series + remote sensing classification: well-matched skill set

Title: Multi-sensor recovery stage classification
Novelty_Justification: Multi-sensor recovery staging (optical + SAR + LiDAR) not published for boreal post-fire landscapes
Tractability_Justification: Three data streams to harmonize spatiotemporally; recovery stage definition needs expert input; sparse ICESat-2 coverage
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; need ABoVE field data for validation; moderate compute; multi-sensor alignment is non-trivial engineering
Confidence_Justification: Multi-sensor should improve over single-sensor but depends on SAR and LiDAR adding genuinely orthogonal information at this scale
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Recovery staging is more ecologically useful than binary recovered/not-recovered classification
Skill_Fit_Justification: Multi-sensor fusion + temporal deep learning: core ML/RS skill set

Title: Spectral-carbon recovery link at flux towers
Novelty_Justification: The specific question — does spectral recovery predict NEE recovery after fire — has not been systematically tested across tower sites
Tractability_Justification: Limited to ~8-12 post-fire boreal tower sites; small sample size constrains statistical power and generalizability
Feasibility_Justification: ICOS/FLUXNET data available (some with access restrictions); satellite data open; limited sites restrict scope
Confidence_Justification: Analysis is straightforward regression but small sample may limit generalizability; individual tower results may not scale
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Directly tests a key assumption in post-fire carbon accounting that affects national carbon inventories
Skill_Fit_Justification: Statistical analysis + satellite-tower comparison; less ML-intensive than other ideas; more data science than engineering

Title: Boreal SIF-GPP calibration network
Novelty_Justification: Multi-site boreal SIF-GPP calibration does not exist; Pierrat (2022) calibrated at one site only
Tractability_Justification: TROPOMI at 3.5×7 km footprint may be too coarse for individual tower comparison; spatial mismatch is a known challenge
Feasibility_Justification: TROPOMI and ICOS data available; need to navigate FLUXNET access policies; limited number of boreal post-fire tower sites
Confidence_Justification: SIF-GPP regression is standard analysis but the boreal-specific relationship may be too site-dependent to generalize
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Calibration step that enables future SIF-based monitoring rather than an end product itself; foundational but not directly impactful
Skill_Fit_Justification: Statistical analysis + satellite data processing; less ML than other ideas; standard remote sensing science

Title: SIF anomaly drought early warning system
Novelty_Justification: No SIF-based drought early warning system exists for any biome including boreal
Tractability_Justification: TROPOMI SIF only since 2018 — 7-year record makes climatological anomaly detection weak; drought events rare in this window
Feasibility_Justification: Open data; low-moderate compute; standard anomaly detection framework
Confidence_Justification: Short baseline (7 years) weakens climatology; 2025 study showed SIF-stomatal decoupling in drought undermines the core assumption
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Drought early warning has direct forest management value; fills gap left by sparse weather station networks in boreal zone
Skill_Fit_Justification: Time series analysis + anomaly detection: reasonable ML/data science match

Title: SIF + LST fusion for drought mechanism
Novelty_Justification: SIF-LST fusion for drought mechanism classification proposed for tropical/Mediterranean but not applied to boreal forests
Tractability_Justification: Requires co-located SIF + LST data; ECOSTRESS has irregular ISS-orbit revisit; spatial and temporal alignment is challenging
Feasibility_Justification: ECOSTRESS data access through NASA; need tower energy balance data for validation; multi-source data fusion is complex
Confidence_Justification: Conceptually sound but SIF-LST phase relationship may be too noisy at TROPOMI resolution; mechanism classification is ambitious
Ecological_Impact_Justification: Distinguishing heat stress from moisture deficit drought informs forest management response and mortality prediction
Skill_Fit_Justification: Multi-sensor fusion + statistical analysis: reasonable skill match; requires some atmospheric science knowledge
